ei.title: Post-event Information Can Distort A Witness's Memory
ei.subject: 11월_2023 고2 모의고사
ei.lesson: Post-event Information Can Distort A Witness's Memory

fullPassage: Information encountered after an event can influence subsequent remembering. External information can easily integrate into a witness's memory, especially if the event was poorly encoded or the memory is from a distant event, in which case time and forgetting have degraded the original memory. With reduced information available in memory with which to confirm the validity of post-event misinformation, it is less likely that this new information will be rejected. Instead, especially when it fits the witness's current thinking and can be used to create a story that makes sense to him or her, it may be integrated as part of the original experience. This process can be explicit (i.e., the witness knows it is happening), but it is often unconscious. That is, the witness might find himself or herself thinking about the event differently without awareness. Over time, the witness may not even know the source of information that led to the (new) memory. Sources of misinformation in forensic contexts can be encountered anywhere, from discussions with other witnesses to social media searches to multiple interviews with investigators or other legal professionals, and even in court.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
① influence: 사건 이후 정보가 기억에 '영향을 미친다' — 적절
② isolate(고립시키다) → integrate(통합하다): 외부 정보가 목격자의 기억에 '통합'되는 맥락에서 isolate는 반대 의미 ←정답
③ degraded: 시간이 원래 기억을 '저하'시켰다 — 적절
④ rejected: 새 정보가 '거부'될 가능성이 낮다 — 적절

This process can be ③<u>explicit</u> (i.e., the witness knows it is happening), but it is often ④<u>intentional</u>. That is, the witness might find himself or herself thinking about the event differently without awareness. Over time, the witness may not even know the source of information that led to the (new) memory. Sources of misinformation in forensic contexts can be encountered anywhere, from discussions with other witnesses to social media searches to multiple interviews with investigators or other legal professionals, and even in court.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
① encoded: 사건이 제대로 '인코딩'되지 않았다 — 적절
② confirm: 기억 정보로 타당성을 '확인'하다 — 적절
③ explicit: 이 과정이 '명시적'일 수 있다 — 적절
④ intentional(의도적인) → unconscious(무의식적인): 목격자가 '무의식적으로' 사건을 다르게 생각하는 맥락에서 intentional은 반대 의미 ←정답

That is, the witness might find himself or herself thinking about the event differently without ④<u>awareness</u>. Over time, the witness may not even know the source of information that led to the (new) memory. Sources of misinformation in forensic contexts can be encountered anywhere, from discussions with other witnesses to social media searches to multiple interviews with investigators or other legal professionals, and even in court.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:

det.analysis:
① evidence(증거): 목격자가 증거 없이 생각한다는 뜻이 아님

(A) Sources of misinformation in forensic contexts can be <u>encountered</u> anywhere, from discussions with other witnesses to social media searches.

(B) The hikers <u>encountered</u> a bear on the trail and slowly backed away.
questions.stem: 다음 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 encountered의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
① (A) 마주치다 — (B) 접하다: 의미가 뒤바뀜
② (A) 접하다 — (B) 접하다: (B)는 곰을 물리적으로 '마주치다'
③ (A) 접하다 — (B) 마주치다: (A) 오정보를 '접하다'(정보 획득) + (B) 곰을 '마주치다'(물리적 대면) ←정답
④ (A) 마주치다 — (B) 마주치다: (A)는 정보를 물리적으로 만나는 것이 아님
det.tip: encountered: (A) 정보를 접하다(come across) vs (B) 동물을 마주치다(meet face to face)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"the quality of being true, real, or based on facts"

det.analysis:
① awareness(인식): 자각 상태이지 사실 기반 속성이 아님
② validity: '진실되거나 사실에 근거한 성질' — 정의 일치 ←정답
③ experience(경험): 겪은 일이지 진실성과 무관
④ memory(기억): 과거 정보 저장이지 타당성이 아님
det.tip: validity = the quality of being true/real = 타당성, 유효성

questions.passage: This process can be explicit (i.e., the witness knows it is happening), but it is often __________. (consciousness)
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: consciousness → unconscious (형용사). explicit(명시적)과 대조되는 '무의식적인' 형태가 필요. consciousness(명사, 의식) → conscious(형용사) → unconscious(형용사, un- 부정 접두사)
det.tip: consciousness → conscious → unconscious. but 이후 대조 관계에 주목

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: integration → integrate (동사). can 뒤에 동사원형이 필요. integration(명사, 통합) → integrate(동사, 통합하다). 조동사 can + 동사원형 구조
det.tip: integration → integrate. 조동사(can) 뒤에는 반드시 동사원형

questions.passage: Information encountered after an event can influence subsequent remembering. External information can easily integrate into a witness's memory, especially if the event was poorly encoded or the memory is from a distant event, in which case time and forgetting have degraded the original memory. With reduced information available in memory with which to confirm the validity of post-event misinformation, it is less likely that this new information will be rejected. Instead, especially when it fits the witness's current thinking and can be used to create a story that __________ to him or her, it may be integrated as part of the original experience. This process can be explicit (i.e., the witness knows it is happening), but it is often unconscious. That is, the witness might find himself or herself thinking about the event differently without awareness. Over time, the witness may not even know the source of information that led to the (new) memory. Sources of misinformation in forensic contexts can be encountered anywhere, from discussions with other witnesses to social media searches to multiple interviews with investigators or other legal professionals, and even in court.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
① falls apart(무너지다): 이야기를 만들 수 있다는 긍정적 문맥에 반함
② makes sense: 그/그녀에게 '이치에 맞는' 이야기를 만든다 — 문맥 일치 ←정답
③ sounds familiar(익숙하게 들리다): 친숙함이 아닌 논리적 일관성이 핵심
④ proves wrong(틀렸음이 증명되다): 이야기 구성과 반대 의미
det.tip: makes sense = 이치에 맞다, 말이 되다. 새 정보로 일관된 이야기를 구성

questions.passage: Information encountered after an event can influence subsequent remembering. External information can easily integrate into a witness's memory, especially if the event was poorly encoded or the memory is from a distant event, in which case time and forgetting have degraded the original memory. With reduced information available in memory with which to confirm the validity of post-event misinformation, it is less likely that this new information will be rejected. Instead, especially when it fits the witness's current thinking and can be used to create a story that makes sense to him or her, it may be integrated as part of the original experience. This process can be explicit (i.e., the witness knows it is happening), but it is often unconscious. That is, the witness might find himself or herself thinking about the event differently without awareness. Over time, the witness may not even know __________ that led to the (new) memory. Sources of misinformation in forensic contexts can be encountered anywhere, from discussions with other witnesses to social media searches to multiple interviews with investigators or other legal professionals, and even in court.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
① the accuracy of testimony(증언의 정확성): 정확성이 아닌 출처를 모른다는 맥락
② the details of the crime(범죄 세부사항): 범죄 세부사항이 아닌 정보 출처가 주제
③ the identity of the witness(목격자 신원): 목격자 자신의 기억 문제이지 신원과 무관
④ the source of information: 시간이 지나 정보의 '출처'를 알 수 없게 된다 — 문맥 일치 ←정답
det.tip: the source of information = 정보의 출처. 기억이 변형된 후 그 출처를 잊게 됨
